summary.signal: 航空・製造ではAI単体より、実機に近いsimulation、複合計測、CT、数値parityといった検証可能なengineering loopへの組み込みが強い。
Scientific AIは、材料文献の大規模構造化とdomain-specific expert AIを通じて、学習モデルを研究データ生成・整理・実験計画へ接続する方向へ進んでいる。
Enterprise Agentではlong-horizon execution、multi-agent orchestration、governed supply-chain dataが実装論点となり、単発chatから継続業務へ重心が移っている。
企業AIでは利用拡大と同時にgovernance gapとbudget overrunが顕在化しており、統制・可視化・費用設計がROI回収の前提条件になっている。

central_signals: Engineering AIの実用境界は、自律性そのものより検証可能なtool executionとphysical/digital feedback loopで決まる。
Scientific AIでは、専門データを構造化・再利用可能にする基盤整備とdomain-specific modelの組み合わせが重要になっている。
Enterprise Agentの長期実行にはmemoryだけでなく、権限、承認点、orchestration、cost controlが必要になる。
tensions_or_caveats: AECC、Salesforce、Fujitsu、Lumafield、Futurumの性能・成果数値は提供元またはスポンサー側の自己申告として扱う。
LG AI Researchの一次ページはCuratorのWeb再取得で開けず、同日付の複数報道で主要内容を照合したためconfidenceを下げている。
Fujitsu MONAKAのAI inference性能値はベンダー比較であり、独立benchmarkではない。
OneTrustとFuturumはいずれも商用組織による調査で、標本設計や回答バイアスを考慮して方向性として読む。

Agnes-3.0-Flash lacked a reliable publication date on the primary model card and was therefore not promoted to selected/wildcard.
The publication index was last updated on 2026-09-09; duplicate control was supplemented with available receipts through 2026-09-14.

selected.title: Modernizing complex legacy code with AI agents
selected.category: AIエージェント・コーディング・Scientific Software
factual_points: Mistral reports migrating 40,000 lines of a 300,000-line physics-intensive Fortran 77 reservoir simulator to C++ in the first sprint.
The team built a numerical-parity harness before migration and used critical intermediate checkpoints as well as final outputs to verify agreement.
More than 100 agents were used to document the legacy caller-callee tree; the final migration workflow used coder, tester and reviewer agents with human review gates.
Mistral states that fully autonomous translation produced functional but poorly modernized code, while structured multi-agent workflows with human checkpoints gave better code quality.

claims.text: The first sprint migrated 40,000 of 300,000 Fortran 77 lines from a physics-intensive reservoir simulator.
The migration used a numerical-parity harness comparing final outputs and critical intermediate checkpoints before accepting migrated modules.
claims.evidence_location: Building a parity harness before migrating legacy code

claims.text: Mistral reports that a structured coder/tester/reviewer workflow with human checkpoints worked better than full autonomy for this case.
claims.evidence_location: Utilizing the AI agents / applying three principles

selected.why_it_matters: Scientific and engineering software modernization is a high-value Agent use case where semantic correctness is not enough; numerical parity provides a concrete acceptance boundary that can be audited independently of model reasoning.
selected.practical_implication: For legacy CFD/FEA/materials codes, build deterministic state checkpoints and numerical regression tests before assigning migration tasks to agents; use human approval at architecture and merge boundaries.

selected.title: Countdown to A350F first flight: Preparing for the sky
factual_points: The A350F Virtual First Flight consists of 13 simulation sessions of roughly five hours each.
The development flight-test simulator is connected to real aircraft avionics benches, including actual flight controls and digital engine control systems.
Airbus describes the setup as about 90% representative of the physical aircraft, with the freighter-specific aerodynamic model remaining to be proven in flight.
The subsequent certification program targets about 400 flight hours with two aircraft and direct EASA participation.

claims.text: Airbus is running 13 approximately five-hour Virtual First Flight sessions connected to real avionics benches including flight controls and digital engine controls.
claims.evidence_location: Virtual First Flight / Connecting the simulator to real avionics

claims.text: Airbus describes the VFF setup as 90% representative of the physical aircraft and plans a roughly 400-flight-hour campaign.
claims.evidence_location: Connecting the simulator to real avionics / flight-test campaign

claims.text: EASA is monitoring and approving the official flight-test plan and is scheduled to participate directly in performance flights.

selected.why_it_matters: This is a concrete example of certification-oriented digital verification where simulation is not a standalone digital twin demo but is connected to representative hardware, failure scenarios and regulator-facing flight-test planning.
selected.practical_implication: Engineering AI and digital-thread programs should distinguish model fidelity from certification evidence; high-value simulation systems need traceable links to hardware benches, failure cases and formal acceptance plans.

selected.title: AECC Dongan deploys 3D+2D+AI composite inspection for engine-production assembly
factual_points: A newly introduced automated 3D scanning system was used for dimensional inspection on an engine-production line and also supported reverse modeling for more than ten products.
For small lock-tab features in narrow assembly positions, the company reports the original 3D-scan recognition accuracy was about 75%.
The team combined 2D visual measurement with an AI training function and reports achieving 100% recognition after more than a month of tuning.
The resulting workflow uses 3D inspection for overall geometry and 2D+AI for difficult local features.

claims.text: The initial 3D scanning workflow achieved about 75% recognition on small lock-tab inspection tasks.
AECC Dongan reports that combining 2D visual measurement with AI training raised recognition to 100% after iterative tuning.
The team created reverse-engineered models for more than ten products and built a 3D database as part of the deployment.

selected.why_it_matters: The case shows a pragmatic industrial pattern: rather than forcing one sensor modality to solve every inspection problem, geometry and vision are combined and AI is assigned to the failure mode where it adds measurable value.
selected.practical_implication: Inspection automation should be architected around modality-specific strengths and traceability; difficult local features can be routed to 2D/AI while retaining 3D dimensional data for overall conformance and reverse-engineering records.

selected.title: LG unveils expert AI for manufacturing, science and finance
factual_points: LG AI Research announced domain-specific Expert AI systems for manufacturing, science and finance at its September 14 event.
The manufacturing stack includes state prediction and autonomous inspection, while EXAONE Discovery targets materials design and synthesis-result prediction.
LG also described an autonomous experimentation framework intended to connect model recommendations with experimental execution.
The official Scout capture says LG has addressed more than 100 industrial challenge cases; this figure remains a company-reported aggregate.

claims.text: LG AI Research announced domain-specific AI systems spanning manufacturing, science and finance on September 14.
claims.evidence_location: Primary release captured by Scout; independently corroborated by same-day Korea Herald coverage

claims.text: The science portfolio includes EXAONE Discovery for materials-related work and an autonomous experimentation direction.
claims.evidence_location: Primary release captured by Scout; same-day Korean press coverage

selected.why_it_matters: A large industrial group is explicitly separating general-purpose models from factory- and science-specific systems, reinforcing the shift toward proprietary process data, domain validation and closed-loop execution as differentiators.
selected.practical_implication: Manufacturing AI evaluations should measure state prediction, inspection and experimental feedback against domain baselines rather than relying on general LLM benchmarks.

provenance.verification_note: Primary URL was not reopenable in Curator web retrieval; core claims were cross-checked against multiple same-day independent reports.

selected.title: Large language model-enabled automated data extraction for concrete materials informatics
selected.category: Scientific AI・材料インフォマティクス
factual_points: The peer-reviewed pipeline extracts composition-process-property attributes from unstructured materials literature and reports F1 up to 0.98 across evaluated attributes.
The authors report extracting nearly 9,000 records with more than 100 attributes in under one hour from a corpus screened from more than 27,000 publications.
The resulting blended-cement concrete database is openly released, and more than 7,500 records are reported as manually verified in the associated dataset documentation.
All authors are inventors on a pending Rice University provisional patent covering the extraction pipeline.

claims.text: The extraction pipeline reaches F1 scores up to 0.98 and produced nearly 9,000 records with more than 100 attributes from over 27,000 screened publications.
The associated open database documentation reports that more than 7,500 records, over 80% of the final database, were manually verified.

selected.why_it_matters: Materials AI often fails before modeling because experimental data remain trapped in literature. This work addresses the data-infrastructure bottleneck directly and exposes both benchmark and production datasets for external reuse.
selected.practical_implication: Materials organizations can evaluate LLM extraction as a data-engineering layer, but should retain human-audited benchmark sets, provenance to source papers and explicit treatment of missing values before downstream model training.

selected.title: Introducing Saturn: Large-Format CT for the Parts You Couldn't Scan Before
factual_points: Saturn provides a 580 mm diameter by 1,100 mm tall scannable volume with a 225 kV source.
Lumafield states the system can penetrate up to 100 mm of light metal and 25 mm of steel or iron, depending on the inspection case.
The Voyager environment supports porosity, wall-thickness and CAD comparison workflows plus automated dimensional feature extraction for GD&T-related checks.
The aerospace use cases explicitly include turbine components, structural weldments and metal-additive parts.

claims.text: Saturn has a 580 mm by 1,100 mm scan volume and a 225 kV source aimed at larger and denser components.
Lumafield positions Saturn for aerospace turbine components, structural weldments and additive parts, with Voyager supporting CAD comparison and dimensional analysis.
claims.evidence_location: Aerospace and defense / connected platform sections

selected.why_it_matters: Large-format CT closes an inspection gap between lab-scale metrology and destructive sectioning for dense aerospace components, while linking volumetric NDI data directly to CAD and dimensional workflows.
selected.practical_implication: For castings, weldments and additive hardware, CT can be evaluated not only as NDI but as a design/manufacturing feedback source feeding CAD comparison, porosity and GD&T analytics in the same dataset.

provenance.publication_history_note: Lumafield Quality Agent was published on 2026-09-09, but Saturn is a separate September 10 hardware/platform release with a different primary URL and distinct large-format CT capability; treated as a material new event.

selected.title: The OneTrust 2026 AI-Ready Governance Survey Report
selected.category: 企業AI・ガバナンス調査
factual_points: OneTrust and Sapio Research surveyed 1,200 senior decision-makers across eight markets in June and July 2026; all respondents worked at organizations with at least $100 million annual revenue.
87% say their organizations encourage AI-agent use, while 47% report clear governance, oversight and controls for that use.
Only 5% report clear coordination and accountability across the AI lifecycle.
86% report at least one AI-related incident in the prior year; among those, 45% implemented formal AI review and approval processes.

claims.text: The survey covered 1,200 senior decision-makers in eight markets during June-July 2026, all from organizations with at least $100 million annual revenue.
87% encourage AI-agent use but only 47% report clear governance, oversight and controls.
claims.evidence_location: Agent Adoption Is Exposing the Next Governance Gap

claims.text: 86% report at least one AI-related incident in the prior year.

selected.why_it_matters: The report quantifies a specific operational gap: organizations are opening Agent access faster than they are connecting governance, visibility and accountability across the AI lifecycle.
selected.practical_implication: Enterprise Agent programs should measure sanctioned/unsanctioned use visibility, approval coverage and incident-response controls alongside adoption metrics; usage growth alone is not readiness.

report_details.methodology: Survey of senior business decision-makers conducted in June-July 2026 with equal representation from CPO, CDO, CISO and CMO audiences; respondents worked at organizations with at least $100M annual revenue.
report_details.geographies: Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Singapore, Spain, United Kingdom and United States
key_metrics: 5% report clear coordination and accountability across the AI lifecycle
86% experienced at least one AI-related incident in the prior year
48% report clear visibility into both sanctioned and unsanctioned AI use
report_details.comparison_to_previous: The public report page does not expose a directly comparable prior-year series; treat this as a 2026 cross-sectional baseline rather than a trend estimate.
report_details.practical_meaning: Agent adoption is materially ahead of lifecycle governance and visibility, making approval, monitoring and ownership the operational bottlenecks.
report_details.caveats: Commissioned/published by a governance software vendor; self-reported survey responses and incident definitions may vary by respondent, and results should not be treated as a census of all enterprises.

selected.title: Salesforce expands Agentforce with long-horizon runtime and multi-agent orchestration
factual_points: Salesforce introduced a long-horizon runtime intended to keep Agentforce goals active across days and weeks rather than single interactions.
The runtime uses persistent memory, durable execution and dynamic steering; Salesforce describes explicit guardrails for autonomous action versus seller approval.
Multi-Agent Orchestration is generally available, while Agent Optimizer is announced for general availability in October 2026.
The release explicitly warns that some referenced services or features may still be in development, so current and future capabilities must be separated.

claims.text: Salesforce introduced a long-horizon runtime that preserves progress across sessions and supports work over days or weeks.
claims.evidence_location: Take on work that spans days and weeks

claims.text: Multi-Agent Orchestration is GA; Agent Optimizer is announced for GA in October 2026.
claims.evidence_location: Take agents further with the Agentforce platform

selected.why_it_matters: Long-running Agent systems need durable state, explicit human-approval boundaries and orchestration across specialized roles; these are operating-system concerns, not merely model capability upgrades.
selected.practical_implication: When evaluating enterprise Agents, test interruption/resume behavior, approval escalation, traceability and multi-agent handoffs over multi-day workflows rather than only single-session task success.

provenance.publication_history_note: Salesforce Headless 360/MCP capabilities were published on 2026-09-02; this September 14 event is a distinct material update centered on long-horizon runtime, durable execution and multi-agent orchestration.

selected.title: Palantir and Fujitsu deepen partnership around governed enterprise AI and FDE
selected.category: 企業AI・製造・データ基盤
factual_points: Fujitsu became a Global FDE Partner for Palantir AIP and Foundry and is investing in Forward Deployed Engineering capability.
Fujitsu says a Japanese manufacturing supply-chain deployment integrates data from more than 3,000 suppliers and 18 factories while retaining governed workflows and access controls.
The release reports more than $10 million in one-year cost savings and doubled operational productivity for the unnamed customer; these are vendor/customer-reported outcomes.
The joint architecture emphasizes customer-controlled deployment, auditing, access controls and sovereign production environments.

claims.text: Fujitsu says the referenced manufacturing deployment integrates data across more than 3,000 suppliers and 18 factories.
Fujitsu reports more than $10 million in cost savings within one year and doubled operational productivity for the unnamed customer.
The partnership explicitly couples Palantir data/ontology workflows with access controls, auditing and customer-controlled deployment environments.

selected.why_it_matters: The manufacturing example makes enterprise AI concrete at supply-chain scale and shows that production deployment is being packaged with data integration, governance and embedded engineering teams rather than model access alone.
selected.practical_implication: Manufacturing AI programs should scope ontology/data harmonization, access-control inheritance and on-site/embedded engineering capacity as first-class deployment workstreams.

selected.title: 46.9% of Enterprises Report AI Spend Over Budget in 2H 2026
factual_points: Futurum reports results from 1,636 global enterprise technology decision-makers.
46.9% report AI spending above plan, compared with 5.6% below plan; 10.0% report having no formal AI budget to compare against.
Among the 767 organizations over plan, 47.6% seek more budget, 43.3% absorb the overrun and 17.2% pause or reduce the AI initiative.
Among organizations reallocating IT budgets, external contractors and consultants are the first reduction for 60.9% of the 297 respondents in that subgroup.

claims.text: The survey includes 1,636 global enterprise technology decision-makers and reports 46.9% of organizations spending above their AI budget plan.
Among 767 over-plan organizations, 47.6% ask for more budget, 43.3% absorb the overrun and 17.2% pause or reduce the initiative.

selected.why_it_matters: AI cost pressure is no longer only a model-pricing problem; organizations are reallocating labor and business-unit budgets to sustain usage, which can obscure true ROI if consumption governance is weak.
selected.practical_implication: AI programs should establish budget owners, unit-cost telemetry and stop/scale criteria before usage expands; otherwise overruns become normalized and are funded by unrelated cost reductions.

report_details.methodology: 2H 2026 CIO & Technology Buyers survey of global enterprise technology decision-makers; the public release reports subgroup counts but does not expose detailed sampling frame, weighting or fieldwork dates.
report_details.geographies: Global; detailed country composition is not disclosed on the public release page.
key_metrics: 47.6% of over-plan organizations request more budget
17.2% of over-plan organizations pause or reduce the AI initiative
report_details.comparison_to_previous: No directly comparable prior-wave metric is exposed in the public release; interpret the figures as a 2H 2026 snapshot.
report_details.practical_meaning: AI consumption is outrunning formal budgeting at many respondents, shifting governance from project approval toward ongoing cost allocation and unit economics.
report_details.caveats: Commercial research-provider survey; sampling frame, weighting and response-rate details are not public on the release page, and spending figures are self-reported.

selected.title: Fujitsu launches FUJITSU-MONAKA and made-in-Japan MONAKA Server for sovereign AI infrastructure
factual_points: Fujitsu announced global sales of FUJITSU-MONAKA and the MONAKA Server from November 2026.
The company describes FUJITSU-MONAKA as a Japan-developed 2nm 3D-stacked CPU and positions the server for AI inference, enterprise and academic/HPC workloads.
MONAKA Server is designed and manufactured in Japan and is positioned for sovereign-AI requirements including traceability and supply-chain transparency.
Fujitsu claims twice the AI inference throughput and lower power requirements versus unspecified comparison CPUs; this is a vendor benchmark and not independently reproduced.

claims.text: Fujitsu announced November 2026 global sales for FUJITSU-MONAKA and MONAKA Server, targeting Japan and Europe among initial server markets.
Fujitsu describes the processor as a Japan-developed 2nm 3D-stacked CPU and positions domestic manufacturing as supporting traceability and sovereign deployment.
Fujitsu claims twice the AI inference throughput and reduced server/power requirements compared with other CPUs.

selected.why_it_matters: The launch broadens sovereign-AI infrastructure beyond GPU procurement to CPU-side inference, domestic manufacturing and traceable server supply chains, which matters for regulated and national-strategy workloads.
selected.practical_implication: Infrastructure comparisons should separate independently measured inference performance from vendor claims and include supply-chain traceability, cooling requirements and deployment geography as evaluation axes.

provenance.verification_note: Release is distributed on PRNewswire but explicitly identifies Fujitsu Limited as the source and links to the full Fujitsu release.

wildcards.title: Bolt Forge uses opt-in build sessions to improve open-model coding agents
wildcards.category: オープンウェイト・コーディングエージェント
factual_points: Forge is an opt-in research-preview coding agent using open models including GLM 5.3 variants, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek v4 Pro.
Bolt says anonymized opted-in build sessions are shared with Arcee AI for future open-weight model training.
Reported benchmark comparisons are project self-evaluations and should not be treated as independent model rankings.

claims.text: Forge is an opt-in research-preview coding agent built around multiple open models.
Bolt states that opted-in anonymized build-session data can be shared with Arcee AI to improve future open-weight models.

wildcards.why_it_matters: It exposes a potentially important open-model flywheel: production coding interactions become training data, but only if consent, anonymization and data-governance boundaries are credible.
wildcards.practical_implication: Track whether open coding-agent ecosystems can build high-quality proprietary interaction datasets without undermining enterprise source-code confidentiality.

wildcards.title: Benchmark Dataset of Vibrational Signals for Artificial Intelligence Applications in Mechanical Systems
wildcards.organization: University of Technology of Troyes collaboration
factual_points: Scientific Data published a benchmark containing 7,000 vibration signals from a modular mechanical transmission system.
The dataset includes induced faults in gears, V-belts and roller chains as well as healthy states and fault propagation across connected modules.
The paper reports that unsupervised statistical and autoencoder baselines show low clustering accuracy, indicating non-trivial diagnostic difficulty.

claims.text: The benchmark contains 7,000 vibration signals with healthy and faulty states across gears, V-belts and roller chains.
The authors report low unsupervised clustering accuracy and poor label alignment for baseline fault-detection methods.

wildcards.why_it_matters: Engineering AI needs realistic benchmark data with interacting components and subtle faults, not only clean single-bearing datasets; this is useful infrastructure for condition-monitoring research.
wildcards.practical_implication: Potential value is highest if future work compares representation-learning and transfer methods under changing load/configuration rather than optimizing against a single fixed fault classifier.

wildcards.title: Light-to-token conversion using MoS2
factual_points: The highlighted work uses a 32x32 MoS2 phototransistor array with FPGA-controlled peripheral circuits for light detection, patching and vector encoding in the analogue domain.
The research highlight reports 87.3% accuracy on a modified CIFAR-10 task and more than 14-fold lower tokenizer energy than a digital implementation.
The Nature Electronics item is a research highlight pointing to the underlying Nature Sensors work, so performance figures should be traced to the original experiment when used publicly.

claims.text: The system uses a 32x32 MoS2 phototransistor array and analogue-domain patch/vector encoding before the digital model stage.
The highlight reports 87.3% modified-CIFAR-10 accuracy and more than 14-fold tokenizer energy reduction versus a digital implementation.

wildcards.why_it_matters: Moving tokenization into the sensor/analogue domain could reduce data movement and preprocessing energy, an increasingly important constraint for edge vision systems.
wildcards.practical_implication: Track whether the energy advantage survives larger arrays, realistic sensor noise and end-to-end workloads; the current result is technically interesting but not yet a general edge-AI architecture proof.
